questions.q:
$A charged particle of mass ‘ $m$ ’ and charge ‘ $q$ ’ moving under the influence of uniform electric field $\overset{→}{\text{E}}\overset{^}{i}$ and a uniform magnetic field $\overset{→}{\text{B}}\overset{^}{k}$ follows a trajectory from point P to Q as shown in figure. The velocities at P and Q are respectively, $v\overset{→}{i}$ and $- 2v\overset{→}{j}$ . Then which of the following statements (A, B, C, D) are the correct? (Trajectory shown is schematic and not to scale)



\left(A\right)E = \dfrac{3}{2} \left(\dfrac{mv^{2}}{qa}\right)$
\left(B\right)$ Rate of work done by the electric field at P is $\dfrac{3}{2} \left(\dfrac{mv^{3}}{a}\right)$
\left(C\right)$ Rate of work done by both the fields at Q is zero
\left(D\right)$ The difference between the magnitude of angular momentum of the particle at P and Q is $2mav$ .$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$( A )$ by work energy theorem

${W}_{mag} + {W}_{ele} = \dfrac{1}{2}m ( 2v{)}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2}m ( v{)}^{2}$

$0 + {qE}_{0}2a = \dfrac{3}{2}{mv}^{2}$
${E}_{0} = \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac{mv2}{qa}$

$( B )$ Rate of work done at $A =$ power of electric force

$= {qE}_{0}V$
$= \dfrac{3}{4}\dfrac{mv3}{a}$

$( C )$ at $Q, \dfrac{dw}{dt} = 0$ for both forces

\left(D\right)$~$\Delta\overset{→}{L} = ( - m2\text{v}2a\overset{^}{k} ) - ( - \text{mvak} )$

$| \Delta\overset{→}{L} | = 3mva$

$

questions.q: Two parallel, long wires are kept $0 . 20m$ apart in vacuum, each carrying current of $xA$ in the same direction. If the force of attraction per meter of each wire is $2 \times {10}^{- 6}N$, then the value of $x$ is approximately
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force per unit length between two parallel wires is& $\dfrac{F}{l} = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}{i}_{1}{i}_{2}}{2\pid}$

Here,~${i}_{1} = {i}_{2} = i$~and~$\dfrac{F}{l} = 2 \times {10}^{- 6}N$

Then,~$2 \times {10}^{- 6} = \dfrac{4{π}^{2} \times {10}^{- 7}i^{2}}{2\pi \times 0 . 2}$

$⇒ i^{2} = \sqrt{2} ⇒ i = 1 . 4A$

Hence,~$x = 1 . 4$.

questions.q: A square loop is carrying a steady current $I$ and the magnitude of its magnetic dipole moment is $m$ . If this square loop is changed to a circular loop and it carries the same current, the magnitude of the magnetic dipole moment of circular loop will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the side of square loop be $a$.
The magnetic dipole is$∴ m = Ia^{2}$
$a = \sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}$
Radius of circular loop $r$ related to $a$ as circumference of circular loop is equal to perimeter of square loop.
$2\pir = 4a = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}$
$r = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}$
$∴$ New dipole moment $m^{'} = \pi{\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{I}}\right)}^{2}I$
$= \dfrac{4m}{\pi}$

$= \dfrac{4m}{\pi}$

questions.q:
A long solenoid is formed by winding $70$~turns ${cm}^{- 1}$ . If $2 . 0A$ current flows, then the magnetic field produced inside the solenoid is ______________.

$( {µ}_{0} = 4\pi \times {10}^{– 7}TmA^{– 1} )$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic field inside solenoid $= {μ}_{o}ni$

where $n =$ Number of turns per unit length

$n = 7000$~turns/m

${B}_{solenoid } = {μ}_{o}ni = 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 7000 \times 2$

$= 8 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times {10}^{- 6} \times 7 \times 100$

$= 176 \times {10}^{- 4}T$

questions.q:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If $\overset{→}{E}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, then the region of space may have :
(A) $E = 0, B = 0$; (B) $E = 0, B e 0$; (C) $E e 0, B = 0$; (D) $E e 0, B e 0$

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force on proton inside an electric and a magnetic field is given by

$\overset{→}{F}e + \overset{→}{F}m = q\overset{→}{E} + q \left(\overset{→}{v} imes \overset{→}{B} ight) . . . \left(1 ight)$

If both $\overset{→}{E}$ and $\overset{→}{B}$ are zero, then $\overset{→}{F}e$ and $\overset{→}{F}m$ both are zero. Hence, velocity may remain constant. Therefore, option (A) is correct.

If $E = 0, B e 0$, but velocity is parallel or antiparallel to the magnetic field, then also $\overset{→}{F}e$ and $\overset{→}{F}m$ both are zero. Hence, option (B) is also correct.

If $E e 0, B e 0$, but $\overset{→}{F}e + \overset{→}{F}m = 0, then also velocity may remain constant. Thus, option (D) is also correct.

$

questions.solution:
Perpendicular distance of centroid from any of the sides will be,& $dtan60 ° = 2\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ d = 2cm$

Each side will subtend an angle of $120 °$~at the centre. Also magnetic field due to all sides will be out of plane of paper, hence total magnetic field can be written as

$B = 3 \times \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{4\pi d} \left[\sin 60 ° + \sin 60 °\right]$

$= 3 \times $\dfrac{{10}^{- 7} \times 2}{2 \times {10}^{- 2}} \times \sqrt{3}

=3\sqrt{3} \times {10}^{- 5}$T

$

questions.q: A metal surface is illuminated by a radiation of wavelength $4500\overset{∘}{A}$. The ejected photo-electron enters a constant magnetic field of $2mT$ making an angle of $90 °$ with the magnetic field. If it starts revolving in a circular path of radius $2$ mm, the work function of the metal is approximately
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the Einstein's photoelectric equation& $K = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - ϕ ⇒ ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - K$

Now~$R = \dfrac{mv}{Bq} ⇒ v = \dfrac{RBq}{m} ⇒ K = \dfrac{R^{2}B^{2}q^{2}}{2m}$

Therefore,~$ϕ = \dfrac{hc}{λ} - \dfrac{R^{2}B^{2}q^{2}}{2m} = \dfrac{6 . 63 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{4500 \times {10}^{- 10}} - \dfrac{\left(2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19}\right)2}{2 \times 9 . 1 \times {10}^{- 31}} ⇒ ϕ = \left(4 . 42 - 2 . 25\right) \times {10}^{- 19}J = \dfrac{2 . 27}{1 . 6}eV = 1 . 36eV$

questions.q: A rectangular coil (Dimension $5cm \times 2.5cm$ ) with $100$ turns, carrying a current of $3A$ in the clock-wise direction, is kept centered at the origin and in the $X - Z$ plane. A magnetic field of $1T$ is applied along $X$-axis . If the coil is tilted through $45 °$ about $Z$-axis , then the torque on the coil is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Torque = \overset{→}{M} \times \overset{→}{B}$
$= MBsin\theta$
$= \left(niA\right)\left(B\right)sin\theta$
$= 100 \times 3 \times \left(5 \times {10}^{- 2} \times 2.5 \times {10}^{- 2}\right) \times 1 \times sin{45}^{o}$
$= 0.27Nm$

questions.q: The magnetic moment of an electron  \left(e\right)$ revolving in an orbit around nucleus with an orbital angular momentum is given by$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}=\mathrm{IA}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{v}}} \pi \mathrm{R}^2\left[\because $\mathrm{I}$=\frac{\mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{V}}}\right]$
$\Rightarrow|\vec{M}|=\frac{1}{2} e v R \Rightarrow|\vec{M}|=\frac{\mathrm{mvR}}{1} \cdot \frac{\mathrm{e}}{2 \mathrm{~m}}$
$\Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=\frac{\mathrm{eL}}{2 \mathrm{~m}} \Rightarrow|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}|=-\frac{\mathrm{e} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}}{2 \mathrm{~m}}$
[ $\because$ Here $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}$ will always be opposite]

questions.q: For a moving coil galvanometer, the deflection in the coil is $0 . 05rad$~when a current of $10mA$ is passed through it. If the torsional constant of suspension wire is $4 . 0 \times {10}^{– 5}Nm{rad}^{- 1}$, the magnetic field is $0 . 01T$ and the number of turns in the coil is $200$, the area of each turn (in ${cm}^{2}$ ) is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:& $\theta = 0 . 05rad, I = 10mA, K = 4 \times {10}^{- 5}Nm{rad}^{- 1}, B = 0 . 01T, N = 200$

The torsional constant of a wire used in a moving coil galvanometer is given by~

$K = \dfrac{NIAB}{θ}$, where,~$A$~is~area of each turn

So,~$A = \dfrac{K\theta}{NIB} = \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{- 5} \times 0 . 05}{200 \times 10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 0 . 01}$

Thus,~$A = {10}^{- 4}m^{2} = 1{cm}^{2}$

questions.q: An insulating thin rod of length $l$ has a linear charge density $ρ\left(x\right) = {ρ}_{0}\dfrac{x}{l}$ on it. The rod is rotated about an axis passing through the origin  \left(x = 0\right)$ and perpendicular to the rod. If the rod makes $n$ rotations per second, then the time averaged magnetic moment of the rod is:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\omega = 2\pi nrads^{- 1}$



$dQ = ρdx$

$= \dfrac{ρ0}{l}xdx$

Current due to elementary charge $dQ$

$dI = \dfrac{dQ\omega}{2\pi}$

Magnetic dipole moment

$dM = dI \times A$

$∫ dM = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{l}\dfrac{ω}{2\pi} \times \dfrac{ρ0}{l} \times xdx\pix^{2}$

$M = \dfrac{{\pinρ}_{0}l^{3}}{4}$

questions.q:
As shown in the figure, a metallic rod of linear density $0 . 45kgm^{- 1}$ is lying horizontally on a smooth incline plane which makes an angle of $45 °$ with the horizontal. The minimum current flowing in the rod required to keep it stationary, when $0 . 15T$ magnetic field is acting on it in the vertical upward direction, will be

(Use $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the wire to remain stationary, the net force acting on it should be zero.

Balancing the forces along the incline,

$mgsin45 ° = ILBcos45 °$

$⇒ I = \left(\dfrac{m}{L}\right)\dfrac{g}{B}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{\left(0 . 45\right)\left(10\right)}{0 . 15} = 30A$

questions.q:
An infinitely long hollow conducting cylinder with radius $R$~carries a uniform current along its surface.

Choose the correct representation of magnetic field \left(B\right)$as a function of radial distance \left(r\right)$& from the axis of cylinder.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Ampere's law,

$∮ \overset{→}{B} \cdot d \overset{→}{l} = {μ}_{0}i$

Inside the hollow cylinder, current will be zero. Therefore, magnetic field will also be zero.

Outside the cylinder,

$B2\pir = {μ}_{0}i ⇒ B = \dfrac{{μ}_{0}i}{2\pir} ⇒ B ∝ \dfrac{1}{r}$

Hence, the correct answer is D.

questions.solution:
velocity along the plate will not change.

$∴ {v}_{1}cos\alpha = {v}_{2}cos\beta$

$\dfrac{K1}{{K}_{2}} ⇒ {v}_{1}^{2}{v}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{\cos^{2}\beta}{\cos^{2}\alpha}$

questions.q: An electron moves through a uniform magnetic field $\overset{→}{B} = {B}_{0}\overset{^}{i} + 2{B}_{0}\overset{^}{j}T$. At a particular instant of time, the velocity of electron is $\overset{→}{u} = 3\overset{^}{i} + 5\overset{^}{j}ms^{- 1}$. If the magnetic force acting on electron is $\overset{→}{F} = 5e\overset{^}{k}N$, where $e$ is the charge of electron, then the value of ${B}_{0}$ is ____ $T$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Force acting on a charged particle under the magnetic field is given by, $\overset{→}{F} = q \left(\overset{→}{v} \times \overset{→}{B}\right).

$⇒ 5e\overset{⏜}{k} = e \left($3\overset{⏜}{i} + 5\overset{⏜}{j}\right)$\times \left({B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{i} +$2{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{j}\right)$

$⇒ 5e\overset{⏜}{k} = e \left(6{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{k} - 5{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{k}\right)$

$⇒ {B}_{0} = 5T

$

questions.q: A single turn current loop in the shape of a right angle triangle with sides $5cm, 12cm, 13cm$ is carrying a current of $2A$. The loop is in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0 . 75T$ whose direction is parallel to the current in the $13$ cm side of the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic force on the $5$ cm~side will be $\dfrac{x}{130}N$. The value of $x$ is _______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here,& $B = 0 . 75T$

The magnitude of magnetic force on the~$5$ cm~side is~${F}_{AB} = i \times \left({l}_{AB}\rright)Bsin\theta \left(\text{angle between}$AC \text{ and } AB\right)$

$= 2 $\times \left(\dfrac{5}{100}\right) \times0 . 75 $\times $\dfrac{12}{13}$

$= \dfrac{9}{130}N$

Hence, the value of~$x = 9.

$

questions.q: A uniform conducting wire of length is $24a,$~and resistance $R$ is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of an equilateral triangle of side $a$ and then in the form of a square of side $a$.~The coil is connected to a voltage source ${V}_{0} .$~The ratio of magnetic moment of the coils in case of equilateral triangle to that for square is $1: \sqrt{y}$ where $y$ is ____________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$4a{n}_{1} = 24a$

thus~${n}_{1} = 6$~turns

$3{an}_{2} = 24a ⇒ {n}_{2} = 8$~turns

$\dfrac{M1}{M2} = \dfrac{{n}_{1}i{A}_{1}}{{n}_{2}i{A}_{2}} = \dfrac{6 \times a^{2}}{8 \times a^{2} \times \dfrac{3}{4}} = \dfrac{3}{1}$

$\dfrac{M2}{M1} = \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{y}$

$y = 3$

questions.q: A circular coil having 200 turns, $2.5 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2$ area and carrying $100 \mu \mathrm{A}$ current is placed in a uniform magnetic field of 1T. Initially the magnetic dipole moment $(\vec{M})$ was directed along $\vec{B}$. Amount of work, required to rotate the coil through $90^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ from its initial orientation such that $\vec{M}$ becomes perpendicular to $\vec{B}$, is ______ $\mu \mathrm{J}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: We know $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{W}_{\text {ext }} & =\Delta \mathrm{U}+\Delta \mathrm{KE} \quad(\text { P.E. }=-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}) \\ & =-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{f}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{M}} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}_{\mathrm{i}}+0 \\ & =-\mathrm{MB} \cos 90+\mathrm{MB} \cos 0 \\ & =\mathrm{MB} \\ & =\mathrm{NIAB} \\ & =200 \times 100 \times 10^{-6} \times \frac{5}{2} \times 10^{-4} \times 1=5 \mu \mathrm{J} \end{aligned}$
